desc:
The string words holds lowercase words of equal length separated by single commas, for example "tars,rats,arts,star". Words may repeat.

Two words are similar if they are identical, or if exchanging exactly two letters (at two different positions) of one word turns it into the other. A group is a set of words in which every word is similar to at least one other word of the set, and the set cannot be extended: words are in the same group when they are linked by a chain of similar words, even if the two ends of the chain are not similar themselves.

Return the number of groups.

"tars,rats,arts,star" -> 2   (tars~rats, rats~arts; star is similar to none of them)
"abc,abc"            -> 1   (identical words are similar)
"abc,bca"            -> 2   (they differ in all 3 positions)
constraints: All words have the same length, between 1 and 10
Words consist of lowercase English letters
hints: Build a graph whose vertices are the words and whose edges connect similar words. You are counting its connected components.
Comparing every pair costs O(w² · L). Two words are similar when they differ in exactly 0 or 2 positions, and in the two positions the letters are crossed.
Alternatively, for each word try all L(L-1)/2 letter exchanges and look the resulting word up in a dictionary of the input words. Union-find merges the matches.
editorial: Union-find over the word indices turns the problem into counting roots. The pairwise approach checks each pair of words for similarity: collect the positions where they differ; the pair is similar if there are none, or exactly two positions i, j with a[i] = b[j] and a[j] = b[i]. That is O(w² L).

With few words and short lengths the second approach is much faster: map every distinct word to its first index, then for each word generate all L(L-1)/2 words obtained by exchanging two letters and union the word with the index of each result that exists in the map (identical words are unioned through the map too). That costs O(w L³) with strings of length L, independent of the number of word pairs.
